svg.text: the line between what a machine can re-fetch and what only the player can supply
item_uid TEXT NN merge hint - indexed, NOT unique
item_type TEXT NN CHECK = 'game' <- the whole door
provider_id TEXT NN } UNIQUE - the upsert's conflict target
acquisition TEXT NN CHECK digital | physical
title / sort_title / search_title TEXT NN two derived, two jobs
playtime_minutes INTEGER NULL NULL = source cannot know
last_played_at TEXT NULL NULL = not reported
owned_since TEXT NULL YYYY | YYYY-MM | YYYY-MM-DD
absent_since TEXT NULL tombstone, NEVER a delete
last_synced_at TEXT NULL PER ROW - a PARTIAL run leaves gaps
item_user TRUTH - only the player writes here
item_id PK, FK item(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
status_manual TEXT NULL NULL = derive on read
status_changed_at TEXT NULL survives a CLEAR - Phase 4 LWW
rating INTEGER NULL Phase 2 writes it
notes TEXT NULL Phase 2 writes it
1:1, materialised by trigger. The sync's UPSERT
CANNOT erase a status: the statement cannot
name a column in this table.
DERIVED, never stored. NULL playtime and 0 playtime
both fall to not_started - which is what derive() returns
for both, so the derivation needs nothing from code.
NO history table, so no retention
column - its absence IS the rule.
mood_tag id PK · key UNIQUE · label
the ONE place the line is a column,
THE LINE IS A TABLE BOUNDARY, NOT A CONVENTION.
A sync writes item, and only item. It cannot destroy a status, a note or a rating, because the UPSERT statement cannot NAME a column in item_user.
A physical row needs no separate guard: physical implements Provider and NOT Syncer, so no sync statement ever reaches it. D1 is what makes this rule enforceable.
Measured cost of the split: +9.8 us on the root screen's page query, +128 us on a whole cold open of 400 titles. Cold open total: 842 us.
NO FK FROM item.provider_id TO provider_connection - DELIBERATELY.
A connection is a relationship the player can END; the library outlives it. An FK would force a choice between deleting a library on
disconnect and forbidding disconnect while items exist. Both are wrong, so there is no FK. The association resolves in code, against
the compiled-in provider registry - which ADR-0001 D1 makes the authority anyway (Capabilities, never the database).
KEY violet = identity and provider replica · green = TRUTH, only the player writes it · gold = CACHE, safe to discard, every
row stamped with its age · blue = sync bookkeeping · grey = local-only, never syncs · red = outside the library file
ZERADO PHYSICAL MODEL - TRUTH, REPLICA, CACHE
Phase 1 DDL. The sync statement cannot name a truth column.
